items.title: Second Circuit revives an LVMH employee’s retaliation claim while preserving arbitration of earlier-accrued claims
items.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
items.summary: The court held that an employee plausibly alleged retaliation after refusing to meet with a supervisor about settling her discrimination claims, treating that refusal as protected activity and the surrounding termination facts as enough to support an inference of retaliation. It nevertheless held that the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act did not undo arbitration for claims that accrued before the law took effect. The judgment was affirmed in part, vacated in part, and remanded.

items.title: Second Circuit limits immediate restitution turnover where the defendant is complying with a payment schedule
items.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
items.summary: In litigation arising from the IIG investment-fraud case, the court held that the government was not entitled to a turnover order for the full value of specified assets while Martin Silver was current on the restitution payment schedule set by the judgment. Silver had made the required $40,000 payment and was not in default. The ruling draws a practical boundary between the government’s broad restitution-enforcement tools and a sentencing court’s express installment schedule.

items.title: Second Circuit holds that border agents need no individualized suspicion for a manual cellphone search
items.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
items.summary: The court held that the border-search exception permits a manual search of a traveler’s cellphone without a warrant or individualized suspicion, and that the First Amendment supplies no separate warrant requirement. The majority treated the phone as property subject to the traditional border power; a concurrence questioned the breadth of that reasoning given the volume of personal information phones contain. The court also affirmed the challenged sentencing enhancements.

items.title: Second Circuit finds no private federal action to enforce No Surprises Act payment awards
items.publisher: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
items.summary: The court affirmed dismissal of a medical provider’s effort to enforce independent-dispute-resolution awards against Cigna. It held that the No Surprises Act does not imply a private right of action for payment enforcement, assigning enforcement instead to federal agencies and states. Although the statute incorporates Federal Arbitration Act standards for vacating an award, the court said it does not incorporate the FAA’s confirmation procedure. The decision clarifies a consequential gap between winning an award and collecting it.

items.title: August state labor data show broad stasis, with unemployment lower in only eight states and D.C.
items.summary: Unemployment rates fell in eight states and the District of Columbia in August and were statistically unchanged in 42 states; the national rate held at 4.1 percent. Payroll employment rose significantly in only four states and was unchanged in the rest plus D.C. Compared with a year earlier, only eight states recorded significant payroll gains. New York’s unemployment rate was 4.3 percent, while D.C. employment was down 27,000, or 3.6 percent, over the year.

items.title: U.S. import and export prices rebound sharply in August, extending large year-over-year gains
items.summary: Import prices rose 0.7 percent in August after falling 0.3 percent in July, while export prices increased 0.6 percent after a 1.4 percent decline. Over twelve months, import prices were up 7.0 percent and export prices 8.6 percent. The release provides a useful upstream inflation signal because these indexes measure prices at the border rather than what consumers ultimately pay, and the simultaneous rebound on both sides of trade is unusually broad.

items.title: New York City projects unusually strong near-term cash balances after large nonprofit advances
items.summary: The Comptroller projects that New York City’s cash balance will average $11.481 billion over the next four months, more than double the $5.631 billion average in the comparable prior-year period. By September 3, the city had disbursed $3.5 billion in advance payments to human-service organizations, with roughly $1 billion still expected. The forecast is both a liquidity measure and a useful window into how quickly the city is moving contracted-service funding into nonprofit hands.

items.title: New York City ends fiscal 2026 with more cash, but timing effects flatter the apparent improvement
items.summary: Fiscal-year cash receipts reached $148.729 billion, up 3.6 percent, while expenditures rose 2.1 percent to $144.787 billion; the city ended with $16.171 billion in cash, versus $12.229 billion a year earlier. The report cautions that delayed Retiree Health Benefits Trust payments and lower prepayments boosted the closing balance. On an accrual basis, expenditures are expected to exceed revenues by $1.828 billion, making the headline cash increase a poor proxy for the underlying budget position.

items.title: SEC proposes reducing annual-report delivery and filing requirements for proxy solicitations
items.summary: The SEC proposes eliminating the requirement to deliver annual reports to security holders, removing a related incorporation-by-reference delivery deadline, ending filing notices for certain exempt solicitations, and shortening the period for broker searches used to distribute proxy materials. The proposal would materially change how investors receive company information and how issuers run solicitations. It is not yet law; public comments are due November 20, 2026, and the Commission may revise or abandon it.

items.title: SEC proposes ending the federal shareholder-proposal process under Rule 14a-8
items.summary: The SEC proposes rescinding Rule 14a-8, which provides the federal process for placing eligible shareholder proposals in company proxy materials. Shareholder-proposal rights would instead depend on state law and company governing documents. Companion amendments would broaden companies’ discretionary authority to vote proxies on proposals omitted from their materials, while letting individual shareholders withhold that authority for their own shares. This is a proposal, not a final rule; comments are due November 20, 2026.

items.title: FAA proposes inspections for potentially misinstalled Boeing 737 elevator-buss bearings
items.summary: The FAA proposes requiring inspections and corrective work on certain Boeing 737-8, 737-9, and 737-8200 airplanes after finding that elevator-buss-assembly bearings may have been installed incorrectly and without required sealant. Cracking or failure could affect pitch control. The agency estimates that 95 U.S.-registered aircraft would be covered and that the basic inspection would cost $1,955 per aircraft, or $185,725 fleetwide, before any repairs. The directive remains a proposal open to comment.

items.title: New York oversight report identifies billions in potential Medicaid savings, mostly from residency questions
items.publisher: Office of the New York State Comptroller
items.summary: The Comptroller reports that state audits and reviews identified about $3.8 billion in potential Medicaid savings, including $2.6 billion in managed-care premiums for members who may reside outside New York. The annual report also cites $115 million in potential New York State Health Insurance Program savings, $8.9 million in improper vouchers and expenses, and $6.8 million recovered from duplicate payments. These are oversight findings and estimates, not all final recoveries or adjudicated fraud.

items.title: Perseverance observations point to several distinct episodes of water activity on early Mars
items.summary: Perseverance data from Jezero Crater’s Margin Unit indicate a more complicated water history than a single long-lived lake. NASA reports that carbon-dioxide-rich groundwater reacted with olivine to form carbonate-filled fractures, while later lake-related water may have produced silica-rich material. Carbonates and silica can preserve evidence of ancient environments and potential biosignatures. The study can place the alteration events in sequence, but it cannot yet assign absolute dates to them.

items.title: XRISM directly measures a pulsar capturing gas from its supergiant companion’s wind
items.publisher: NASA and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency
items.summary: XRISM’s high-resolution Resolve instrument detected redshifted iron absorption lines in the binary system BP Crucis, showing gas moving toward its pulsar at about 335,000 miles per hour, or 540,000 kilometers per hour. The observation gives researchers a direct view of how a neutron star captures part of a massive companion’s stellar wind, the process that powers the system’s X-ray flares. It also demonstrates the diagnostic precision of the young X-ray observatory.

items.title: Hubble highlights a galaxy whose central structure rotates perpendicular to its outer disk
items.summary: Hubble observations of NGC 4698 show an unusual geometry: the galaxy’s central bulge stretches at roughly a right angle to the disk, and its central stars and gas rotate perpendicular to the outer system. NASA says the arrangement likely records external gas accretion or a minor merger rather than ordinary internal evolution; a short hydrogen tail supports that interpretation. The object offers a compact example of how galaxy structure can preserve evidence of past encounters.
